//: forceExit is retained deliberately and is NOT masking an app leak. --detectOpenHandles across a diverse spec sample (mcp-health, scoped-pool, staleness-event, communities, fact-usage, concurrent-single-active) reports ZERO open handles: app.close() + the OnModuleDestroy hooks (SurrealService et al.) release every resource, so the suite exits cleanly on its own. forceExit stays as the CI-termination backstop that pairs with workerIdleMemoryLimit below: an over-budget worker can be hard-killed (the #78 SIGABRT root cause), and forceExit guarantees the jest parent still terminates instead of hanging the runner. Drop it only after a FULL-suite run without it confirms every spec exits cleanly. --- maxWorkers is Serial (1) on purpose (this note lives under the bare '//' key, which jest ignores; a '//ci' key fuzzy-matched jest's real 'ci' option and warned on every run). The in-process e2e loads native modules (bge-m3 ONNX ~340MB + cross-encoder) per worker; at 50% (=2 on the 4CPU/16GB CI runner) two heavy full-stack suites (memory-injection-redteam / fovea-cascade / memtrap) coexist and exhaust RAM, so the OS SIGABRT-kills a worker (Napi::Error, 'suite failed to run' while every test that ran passed). Recurred after the #344 maxWorkers:50% attempt on memory-injection-redteam specifically. Serial gives each suite the full runner memory; workerIdleMemoryLimit still restarts the worker between files to free native allocations. Locally (more RAM) the full e2e is green at any worker count; this is a CI-memory constraint, not a test bug. --- 2026-08 UPDATE (the Brain v2 wave took the suite to ~105 files and the SIGABRT came back at ~40% of runs). Two claims above were wrong and are corrected here; the settings themselves are kept, the actual cause was removed in the fixture instead. WRONG CLAIM 1 — 'workerIdleMemoryLimit still restarts the worker between files to free native allocations'. It cannot see native allocations at all: jest-worker compares the limit against process.memoryUsage().heapUsed of the worker's MAIN thread only (jest-worker 30.4.1, build/processChild.js sends PARENT_MESSAGE_MEM_USAGE = heapUsed). ONNX arenas and the app's own worker_threads are outside that number. Measured on a full serial run with a per-file RSS probe: peak worker RSS 4433MB against peak heapUsed 1180MB — a '1GB' budget let the worker reach 4.4GB, and still fired often enough to burn 26 worker PIDs over 105 files. WRONG CLAIM 2 — 'locally the full e2e is green at any worker count; this is a CI-memory constraint'. It is not a memory constraint at all, it is native heap CORRUPTION. On the CI runners the line immediately preceding the SIGABRT is glibc's allocator aborting: 'free(): invalid pointer' (runs 32992460923 / 32988759755 / 32973603510) or 'free(): invalid next size (fast)' (run 32987462354) — four failures across four different branches on one day, and never a SIGKILL or an OOM-killer message, which is what actual memory exhaustion produces. Locally on darwin the same fault surfaces through libc++ as 'libc++abi: terminating due to uncaught exception of type Napi::Error' -> SIGABRT; it reproduces at maxWorkers:1 on a 128GB machine, first try, giving the exact CI shape ('Test Suites: 1 failed, 104 passed', 'Tests: 455 passed, 455 total'). WHAT IS ESTABLISHED: the only native addon in the app's loaded graph is onnxruntime-node (via @xenova/transformers); an e2e run spawns 85 cross-encoder + 85 intent-classifier ONNX worker threads, each force-terminated seconds later by app.close(); and removing those spawns removes the abort (4/4 green full runs, 0 aborts). Ruled OUT by audit, so don't re-audit: (a) double-dispose — all four native-worker owners (EmbedderService.onModuleDestroy, CrossEncoderService / IntentClassifierService / LocalNerService.onApplicationShutdown) already read-then-null their worker handle before terminating, so disposal is exactly-once and idempotent; (b) shared/aliased native buffers — src/ contains no SharedArrayBuffer, no postMessage transferList and no allocUnsafe, so every worker RPC payload is structured-CLONED, never shared; (c) the bge-m3 embedder — it is stubbed in e2e and its worker spawns 0 times. LEADING HYPOTHESIS, NOT PROVEN: Worker.terminate() force-disposes the worker isolate while onnxruntime-node is still inside from_pretrained() constructing the InferenceSession, freeing N-API allocations under a running native call. It fits (the bootstrap warmup is fire-and-forget, e2e specs are short, so nearly every boot lands teardown inside the load window; the cold first load is the widest window, and the local repro died on a FRESH worker's FIRST file at 1112MB RSS) — but an isolated harness doing exactly that (120 spawn/terminate-mid-warmup cycles with allocator churn, darwin) did NOT abort, so the corrupting interaction needs the full app context and/or glibc. Pinning the exact call site wants a Linux/glibc container with MALLOC_CHECK_=3 / MALLOC_PERTURB_ (or ASAN); that belongs with the follow-up below, not here. Either way it explains why maxWorkers / workerIdleMemoryLimit only ever moved the failure RATE: they change how often the suite crosses the native teardown path, never whether crossing it is safe. ACTUAL CAUSE — the e2e app was loading models on every boot. The fixture stubbed EmbedderService and ExtractorService but nothing stubbed the two models AppModule warms itself: CrossEncoderService.onApplicationBootstrap fire-and-forgets a warmup that spawns a worker_thread loading Xenova/bge-reranker-base (~279MB ONNX via onnxruntime-node), and IntentClassifierService.onModuleInit does the same for a ~135MB NLI model. Counted by worker-spawn: 85 of each across one run, each torn down seconds later by app.close(). A/B over the same 4 heaviest specs, reranker model reachable vs not: peak RSS 3776MB -> 1146MB, per-file RSS deltas +1601/+1507/+886/+149MB -> +219/+58/+20/+8MB, and heapUsed IDENTICAL in both arms (625MB peak) — i.e. essentially all cross-suite growth was native and unmetered. The abort is that create/destroy churn, not a slow leak: the reproduced one hit a FRESH worker on its FIRST file at 1112MB RSS, immediately after it spawned its first ONNX worker threads. FIX (test-infra only, no src change) — test/app-fixture.ts now also overrides LocalCrossEncoderProvider with StubLocalCrossEncoder and sets CHAT_ROUTE_NLI_ENABLED=false, extending the existing 'no model in the test process' policy to both; the two specs that build their own module instead of calling createApp() (retract-auth, mention-locale) carry the same overrides. The stub returns exactly the branch the real provider takes while its model is still loading — isReady() false, score() [] -> identity permutation — which is what e2e observed anyway, so the rerank stage is still entered and still emits metrics. AFTER — four consecutive local full runs, all green (105/105 suites, 456/456 tests, 0 aborts, 0 ONNX worker spawns each time): peak worker RSS 1470/1595/1501/1514MB (was 4433), largest per-file RSS delta +136MB (was +2122MB), the curve flat at ~1.2-1.6GB instead of sawtoothing to 4.4GB, wall clock 363/309/259/270s (was 382s). CI build-test green on the same change: e2e step 106/106 suites, 465/465 tests, zero free()/Napi/SIGABRT matches in the job log. maxWorkers:1 and workerIdleMemoryLimit:1GB are KEPT as backstops, but note they only ever bound the V8 heap — if a future spec boots a native model again, neither will catch it, and neither addresses the corruption at all. Sharding the CI step was considered and rejected on the same ground: a fresh process per shard halves the RSS peak but the abort landed on a fresh worker's first file, so sharding would not have prevented it. RESIDUAL, PRODUCTION-SIDE (deliberately NOT fixed here — it is a src/ behaviour change and wants its own PR): terminate() still cannot interrupt an in-flight native call safely. Shutting the app down inside the model-warmup window can corrupt the heap in prod too; it is survivable there only because it happens once per process, at exit. The real fix is a graceful drain — post a 'close' message, let the worker return from its current op and exit itself, and fall back to terminate() only after a bounded wait — for all four workers (bge-m3, cross-encoder, intent-classifier, local-ner).
